questions.rationale: Choose PPE for the specific risk.

questions.stem: Is PPE the first or last line of defence?
options: The last line of defence
The first line of defence
The only defence needed
Not a defence at all
questions.rationale: Removing or controlling the hazard comes first. PPE protects against what remains.

questions.stem: Who must provide your PPE under the Sentinel scheme?
options: Your sponsor
You must buy it yourself
The train company
Network Rail for everyone
questions.rationale: Sponsors must provide appropriate PPE.

questions.stem: What should you do if you have not been given the right PPE for a task?
options: Do the task without it, but take extra care
Do not start the task and tell your supervisor
Borrow someone else's that does not fit
Use household items instead
questions.rationale: Report missing PPE.

questions.stem: Why should high-visibility clothing have long sleeves on Network Rail infrastructure?
options: To look smarter in front of members of the public
To cover any tattoos while you are at work
Because it is usually colder on the lineside
To give more visible area and protect your arms
questions.rationale: Network Rail requires orange clothing that covers the arms and legs for most work.

questions.stem: Which of these would make your hi-vis less effective?
options: Keeping it clean and fastened all the way up
Fastening it fully
Wearing it over warm clothes
Carrying a large dark bag that covers it
questions.rationale: Do not cover your hi-vis.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a helmet chinstrap in some situations?
options: To stop the helmet falling off, for example at height
To make the helmet look smarter when worn
To hold your radio close to your ear
To hold your radio close to your ear in noisy areas
questions.rationale: Use chinstraps when the risk assessment says so.

questions.stem: Why should you not wear loose scarves or hoods near passing trains?
options: Slipstream can catch them and pull you
They hide your face
They are against company colour rules
They make you too warm
questions.rationale: Loose clothing can be drawn towards trains or machinery.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to carry a radio or phone on site?
options: Clipped to the rail so that you always know where it is
Clipped to the rail so you know where it is
On the ballast next to where you are working
Secured in a pocket or holder so your hands are free
questions.rationale: Keep your hands free for balance.

questions.stem: What should you check before putting on PPE?
options: That it is a colour you like and looks smart
That it is in good condition, fits and suits the task
That it is brand new and has never been worn
That it is the same make and model as your colleague's kit
questions.rationale: Inspect PPE before use.

questions.stem: What should you do with PPE that has reached the end of its life?
options: Keep using it until it falls apart completely
Repair it with tape so it lasts a bit longer
Lend it to a visitor who has none of their own
Replace it as your employer's arrangements require
questions.rationale: Old PPE may no longer protect you.

questions.stem: Why is reflective tape on hi-vis important at night?
options: It reflects train headlights so you can be seen
It glows in the dark without any light on it
It glows in the dark even without any light on it
It shows your name and employer to drivers
questions.rationale: Retroreflective bands improve night visibility.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT PPE?
options: A safety helmet
A line blockage
Safety boots
Eye protection
questions.rationale: A line blockage is a safe system of work, not PPE.

questions.stem: Why must you not alter or cut your hi-vis clothing?
options: It voids the manufacturer's warranty
It belongs to Network Rail, not to you
It breaks the company's dress code
It can reduce its visibility and protection
questions.rationale: Use PPE as supplied.

questions.stem: When working with chemicals such as weedkiller near the line, what should you use?
options: The PPE specified for that chemical, such as gloves and goggles
No PPE, because the weedkiller is mixed with water first
Only a high-visibility jacket so you can be seen
Only safety boots, as spills land on your feet
questions.rationale: Follow the COSHH assessment.

questions.stem: What does COSHH stand for?
options: Code of Safety for Hazardous Handling
Control of Substances Hazardous to Health
Code of Safety for Handling Hazards
Conductor and Overhead Safety Handling
questions.rationale: COSHH regulations control the use of hazardous substances.

questions.stem: Why might you need a dust mask or respirator?
options: To hide your face from CCTV cameras on the railway
Cutting ballast or concrete can create harmful dust such as silica
To keep your face warm during winter night shifts and stop it getting wet
To let you breathe in tunnels where there is no air
questions.rationale: Use respiratory protection when the task needs it.

questions.stem: What must you do if your respirator does not fit properly?
options: Use it anyway for short jobs only
Not rely on it, and get one that fits
Tape the edges to your face to seal it
Borrow a colleague's for the shift
questions.rationale: Respirators need a proper fit to work.

questions.stem: Which of these is the correct approach to PPE in the hierarchy of control?
options: Use it instead of planning the work
Use it after other controls have reduced the risk
Only use it when a manager is watching
Use it instead of planning, as it is quicker to arrange
questions.rationale: Elimination and engineering controls come first.

questions.stem: Why should your helmet be the right size?
options: Larger helmets are hotter to wear in summer
A loose helmet can fall off and fail to protect you
Smaller helmets look smarter on site
The size does not matter as long as it is worn
questions.rationale: Adjust the helmet for a secure fit.

questions.stem: Why should you report damaged safety boots?
options: Damaged boots may not protect your feet or give grip
So you can get a newer, more fashionable pair
So you can claim money back from your sponsor
So you can claim the cost back from your sponsor
questions.rationale: Your footwear is vital on uneven ground.

questions.stem: Why is a lamp or head torch useful equipment at night?
options: It helps you see the ground, hazards and your route
It warns approaching drivers that they must stop
It replaces the need for high-visibility clothing
It acts as a signal to the lookout that you are safe
questions.rationale: Do not shine it at drivers.

questions.stem: What is the danger of headphones under your helmet?
options: They will get dirty and stop working
They will get dirty and stop working properly
You may not hear warnings or approaching trains
They make the helmet sit too loosely
questions.rationale: Personal headphones are not allowed on or near the line.

questions.stem: Why must you never use PPE as a substitute for a safe system of work?
options: PPE cannot protect you from being struck by a train
PPE is uncomfortable to wear for a full shift
PPE is too expensive to rely on every day
PPE can only be worn by people with a licence
questions.rationale: Only a safe system of work protects you from trains.

questions.stem: What should you do if someone in your group is not wearing required PPE?
options: Remind them, and tell the COSS if they do not put it on
Ignore it, as it is their own responsibility
Lend them your helmet and work without it
Ignore it, as it is their own responsibility to wear the PPE they need
questions.rationale: Everyone looks out for each other.

questions.stem: Why is it important that your hi-vis is not faded?
options: It looks unprofessional to the public
It breaks the law on colours
It is more expensive to wash
Faded colours are less visible
questions.rationale: Replace faded hi-vis.

questions.stem: What does a safety helmet protect against?
options: Electric shock from the overhead line
Electric shock from the overhead line and contact with the conductor rail
Noise from machinery and power tools
Head injuries from falling objects and impacts
questions.rationale: Helmets do not protect against electricity or trains.

questions.stem: Can rubber gloves make it safe to touch the conductor rail?
options: No, never touch the conductor rail
Yes, if they are thick
Yes, if they are new
Yes, if they are thick and in good condition
questions.rationale: Ordinary gloves give no safe protection against live rails.

questions.stem: What should you do if PPE makes it hard to see or hear on site?
options: Remove it without telling anyone
Take it off without telling anyone and carry on
Tell the COSS so arrangements can be changed
Ask a colleague to warn you
questions.rationale: PPE must not create new risks.

questions.stem: Which statement about PPE and visitors is correct?
options: Visitors do not need PPE if they are escorted
Visitors may wear yellow instead of orange
Visitors on or near the line also need correct PPE
Visitors only need a helmet, not hi-vis
questions.rationale: Anyone going on or near the line must wear correct PPE.

questions.stem: What should you wear to protect against cold weather on site?
options: A dark coat worn over the top of your hi-vis jacket
Warm layers worn under or as part of approved orange hi-vis
A dark waterproof coat worn over the top of your hi-vis to keep it dry
No extra layers, as hi-vis keeps you warm enough
questions.rationale: Keep warm without covering your hi-vis.

questions.stem: What PPE might you need when using a disc cutter on rail?
options: Only a hi-vis vest so others can see you working
Only safety boots in case the rail drops
Eye and face protection, hearing protection and gloves
None at all if the cut takes less than a minute
questions.rationale: Cutting creates sparks, noise and debris.

questions.stem: Why should you avoid wearing rings on site?
options: They are against the company uniform rules
They are against the company uniform rules and might get lost in the ballast
They interfere with the signalling system
They can catch on equipment and cause serious injuries
questions.rationale: Jewellery can cause entanglement and conduct electricity.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for wearing your PPE correctly?
options: Only the COSS
Only the sponsor
Only Network Rail
You are
questions.rationale: Your sponsor provides PPE, but you must wear and look after it.

questions.stem: Which statement about PPE and fatigue is correct?
options: Heavy or poorly fitting PPE can add to tiredness, so report it
Wearing PPE prevents fatigue during long shifts
PPE is only needed for people who are already tired
Wearing PPE prevents fatigue during long shifts because it keeps you warm
questions.rationale: Comfortable, well-fitted PPE helps you stay alert.

questions.stem: What should you do with a helmet that has taken a heavy impact?
options: Keep using it if there is no visible crack
Paint over the mark
Replace it, even if it looks fine
Give it to a visitor
questions.rationale: Impact can weaken a helmet without visible damage.

questions.stem: Why might you need a waterproof hi-vis jacket?
options: To keep you afloat when crossing rivers
To insulate you when working under OLE
To replace the need for safety boots
To stay dry and visible in bad weather
questions.rationale: Wet and cold workers are less alert.

questions.stem: Which personal item should you carry on site at all times when working on Network Rail infrastructure?
options: Your passport or driving licence
Your bank card
Your Sentinel card
Your car log book
questions.rationale: You must carry your Sentinel card and show it when asked.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to carry hand tools when walking to site?
options: Loose in your hands so you can drop them quickly
In a tool bag or holder, keeping your hands free
Tucked into your belt with the blades facing out
Balanced on top of your helmet to keep hands free
questions.rationale: Secure tools reduce trip and cut risks.

questions.stem: Before using a power tool on site, what should you check?
options: That it is the newest model available from the store
That it is in good condition, guarded and you are trained
That it is loud enough for others to hear it working
That its colour matches your orange PPE
questions.rationale: Inspect tools before use and report defects.

questions.stem: What should you do with a defective tool?
options: Keep using it carefully until the job is done
Take it out of use, label it and report it
Leave it on the line for the next shift
Give it to a colleague who might fix it
questions.rationale: Defective tools cause injuries.

questions.stem: Why must petrol-driven tools be refuelled carefully on site?
options: Fuel is expensive and should not be wasted on site
Fuel is expensive and should not be wasted on site by spilling it on the ground
Fuel leaves stains on the ballast that look untidy
Fuel is a fire risk near hot engines and electrical equipment
questions.rationale: Refuel with the engine cold and away from ignition sources.

questions.stem: Why should tools never be left on the ballast shoulder of an open line?
options: They may be struck by a train or moved by slipstream
They may get wet and start to rust if it rains
They may be stolen by trespassers walking the line
They may be hard to find when you come back later
questions.rationale: Keep equipment clear of the line.

questions.stem: What is hand-arm vibration (HAV)?
options: Damage to hands and arms from long use of vibrating tools
A warning signal given by a lookout using a vibrating horn
A type of padded glove used with heavy power tools
A track defect caused by vibration from heavy trains
questions.rationale: Limit exposure and report symptoms such as tingling or numbness.

questions.stem: What symptoms might show hand-arm vibration damage?
options: Headaches with no other symptoms
Sore and watering eyes
Sunburn on the backs of the hands
Tingling, numbness or white fingers
questions.rationale: Report symptoms early to your employer.

questions.stem: Which of these helps reduce exposure to vibration?
options: Using low-vibration tools and limiting time on the tool
Holding the tool more tightly to absorb the shaking
Using it for longer without breaks to finish sooner
Wearing thin gloves only so you can grip properly
questions.rationale: Follow your employer's exposure limits.

questions.stem: Why should you use the right tool for the job?
options: The right tool always saves money for the sponsor
The right tool looks more professional on site
The wrong tool can cause injury or damage equipment
The right tool means breaks can be longer
questions.rationale: Improvising with tools is a common cause of injury.

questions.stem: What should you check before using a hand trolley on the line?
options: That it is the lightest one available in the store
That it is authorised, has working brakes and is protected
That it is painted orange so drivers can see it
That it has a radio fitted for calling the signaller
questions.rationale: Trolleys need specific controls because they can run away.

questions.stem: What is the risk of carrying heavy items on uneven ballast?
options: The items will rust if they touch the ballast
The ballast will move and damage the track
You may lose your balance and fall towards the line
The items may be stolen if you put them down
questions.rationale: Use mechanical aids and team lifts where needed.

questions.stem: What should you do before lifting a heavy object on site?
options: Lift it quickly so you spend less time straining
Assess the load and get help or lifting aids if needed
Bend your back and lift with your arms straight
Ask the lookout to help you with the lift
questions.rationale: Manual handling injuries are common on the railway.

questions.stem: Which lifting technique is correct?
options: Bend your knees, keep your back straight and the load close
Bend at the waist with your legs kept straight and locked
Twist your body as you lift to move the load sideways
Hold the load at arm's length so it does not touch you
questions.rationale: Good technique reduces back injuries.

questions.stem: What is a 'team lift'?
options: Two or more people lifting together, with one giving instructions
A lift done by a crane while a team stands nearby watching to make sure it is safe
A lift shared between shifts so each team does part of it
A lift done at night when there are more people available
questions.rationale: Coordinate team lifts clearly.

questions.stem: Why should you check your torch or lamp before a night shift?
options: So you have reliable light to see hazards
So you can use it to signal to trains
So you can make drivers slow down
So you do not need to wear hi-vis
questions.rationale: Bring spare batteries.

questions.stem: Why should you carry water on hot days?
options: To avoid dehydration, which affects concentration
To cool the rails if they get too hot
To put out small fires near the OLE
To cool the rails down if they get too hot in summer sun
questions.rationale: Heat and dehydration make you less alert.

questions.stem: What should you do if your radio battery is running low during work?
options: Keep quiet and hope it lasts the shift
Turn it off to save power until needed
Tell the COSS so communication can be kept up
Keep quiet and hope that it lasts until the end of the shift
questions.rationale: Communication is part of the safe system.

questions.stem: Which of these should never be used as a train warning device?
options: An approved horn
A mobile phone call or text
An approved horn used by a competent lookout
An approved LOWS beacon
questions.rationale: Phones can fail or be missed.

questions.stem: Why must tools be accounted for at the end of work?
options: So nothing is left on the line that could endanger trains
Only to stop tools being stolen from the site
To make the end-of-shift paperwork longer
Only to stop tools being stolen from the site after the group has left
questions.rationale: Items left on the line can cause accidents.

questions.stem: What should you do with waste materials on site?
options: Remove them or store them safely clear of the line
Leave them in the cess for the next shift to clear
Spread them on the ballast so they are flat
Burn them on site, even near the OLE
questions.rationale: Waste can be blown onto the line or block routes.

questions.stem: Why should you not stand on equipment such as rail stacks to reach things?
options: It damages the rails and makes them unusable
It is against the rules on wearing PPE
It is uncomfortable to stand on rails
You could fall, and the stack may be unstable
questions.rationale: Use proper access equipment.

questions.stem: What should you check before using a ladder on site?
options: That it is made of metal so that it is strong enough for the job
That it is the tallest ladder available so you can reach everything
That it has been freshly painted so it can be seen by drivers
That it is sound, suitable and allowed, especially near electrification
questions.rationale: Ladders near OLE need special controls.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a first aid kit on site?
options: To treat minor injuries and help until emergency services arrive
To store small tools and spare parts in a safe place
To replace the need for hospital treatment after injuries
To carry snacks and drinks for the group on long shifts
questions.rationale: Know where the first aid kit is.

questions.stem: Who should be told if you take medication that might affect your use of equipment?
options: Nobody, because medical matters are always private
Only your friends within the work group
Your supervisor or sponsor, under the medication policy
The driver of the next train through the site
questions.rationale: Some medicines make you drowsy.

questions.stem: What should you do if you find a tool left on the line by another team?
options: Keep it, as it has been left behind by its owner
Report it, and only remove it if your safe system allows
Keep it, as it has obviously been left behind by its owner on purpose
Throw it into the cess so it is off the track
questions.rationale: Foreign objects can endanger trains.

questions.stem: Why should you avoid carrying tools on your shoulder near OLE?
options: They will hurt your shoulder
They can come too close to live wires
They may fall off and hit someone behind you
They look untidy
questions.rationale: Keep items low near OLE.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to store sharp tools on site?
options: Blade up on the ballast so it dries out
With guards or covers on, in a safe place
Blade up on the ballast so it dries
In your pocket so it is always handy
questions.rationale: Prevent cuts and trips.

questions.stem: What is the main hazard of using generators on site?
options: They attract trains to slow down nearby
They are too quiet to hear when running
They make the overhead line become live
Fumes, noise, fire and electrical risks
questions.rationale: Use generators in well-ventilated areas and follow guidance.

questions.stem: Why should you not run cables across walking routes without protection?
options: They will be stolen
People could trip over them
The cables will get wet and stop working
They will stop trains
questions.rationale: Manage trip hazards.

questions.stem: What should you do if your gloves reduce your grip on a tool?
options: Remove them for all tasks
Use more suitable gloves for the task
Take the gloves off and use the tool with bare hands
Use tape on the gloves
questions.rationale: Choose gloves for both protection and grip.

questions.stem: When using a disc cutter, why must the guard be fitted?
options: To make the cutter quieter when cutting rail
To protect you from the spinning disc and fragments
To make the cutter lighter and easier to hold
To stop the cutter overheating during long cuts
questions.rationale: Never remove guards.

questions.stem: What is the first thing to do if a power tool starts behaving abnormally?
options: Stop using it and switch it off safely
Keep going to finish quickly
Keep going to finish the job quickly
Hand it to a colleague
questions.rationale: Faulty tools can cause serious injury.

questions.stem: Which of these is good practice when working with others using tools?
options: Keep a safe distance and agree who is doing what
Stand close by to watch and learn the technique
Work in each other's swing area to save space
Use tools without telling others to save time
questions.rationale: Coordinate to avoid injuries.

questions.stem: Why might you need sun protection on long summer shifts?
options: Because PPE blocks the sun
To avoid sunburn and heat illness
To keep high-visibility clothing bright
To see signals better
questions.rationale: Heat illness affects concentration.

questions.stem: Which equipment should be checked to make sure it is in calibration before use?
options: Measuring and testing equipment
Your hi-vis jacket
Your lunch box
Your boots and hi-vis jacket
questions.rationale: Inaccurate measurements can lead to unsafe track.

questions.stem: Why should you keep your personal equipment tidy at the work site?
options: Clutter causes trips, and items can end up on the line
A tidy site looks better in progress photographs
Tidiness is part of the company uniform rules
A tidy site reduces the paperwork at the end
questions.rationale: Good housekeeping prevents accidents.

questions.stem: Which item is useful for emergencies if you are working alone in a permitted way?
options: A newspaper to read during quiet times
A newspaper or magazine to read during the quiet times
A camera to record any defects found
A charged phone and the emergency contact numbers
questions.rationale: You must be able to call for help.

questions.stem: What does PPE stand for?
options: Personal protective equipment
Possession protection equipment
Primary position of escape
Personal possession entry
questions.rationale: PPE protects against hazards that remain after other controls.

questions.stem: Which EN standard class is the minimum visibility class for railway hi-vis under RIS-3279-TOM?
options: Class 1 of EN ISO 20471, the lowest class
Class 2 of EN ISO 20471
Class 5 of EN ISO 20471, the highest class
There is no visibility class for railway clothing
questions.rationale: Railway hi-vis garments must meet at least Class 2.

questions.stem: Why is the colour orange chosen for railway high-visibility clothing?
options: It is the cheapest dye available
It matches the company logo
It stands out against the railway background
It reflects heat away from the body in summer
questions.rationale: Orange contrasts with vegetation and signal colours.

questions.stem: What should you do if your hi-vis trousers are torn at the knee?
options: Keep wearing them until they fall apart
Replace them
Cut them into shorts
Cover the hole with a dark patch
questions.rationale: Damaged PPE should be replaced.

questions.stem: Why should safety boots have a good tread?
options: To make them look newer
To grip on ballast and wet surfaces
To make the boots lighter and easier to walk in
To make them quieter
questions.rationale: Slips near the line are dangerous.

questions.stem: What is a 'midsole' in safety footwear for?
options: Protection against sharp objects through the sole
Keeping your feet warm in winter
Making the boot more flexible
Keeping your feet warm on cold winter night shifts
questions.rationale: Midsoles help prevent puncture injuries.

questions.stem: What should you wear when using a strimmer near the line?
options: Only a hi-vis vest
Eye, face and hearing protection as assessed
Only a hi-vis vest so that the driver can see you
Nothing extra
questions.rationale: Strimmers throw debris and are noisy.

questions.stem: What PPE might be needed for working in a tunnel?
options: Only sunglasses for when you come out of the tunnel into daylight
Only sunglasses for when you come out of the tunnel
Suitable lighting, hi-vis and other items set by the risk assessment
No extra PPE, as tunnels are sheltered
questions.rationale: Tunnel work needs specific planning.

questions.stem: Why should you not wear your own non-approved hi-vis on Network Rail sites?
options: It might be a nicer colour
It may not meet the railway standard
It might be more comfortable
It might be cheaper than the approved type
questions.rationale: Railway hi-vis must meet RIS-3279-TOM.

questions.stem: What should you check on a helmet before use?
options: The colour of the inside padding
Cracks, damage and the expiry date
The brand of the strap
Whether it matches your boots
questions.rationale: Helmets degrade over time.

questions.stem: Why might a helmet need replacing even without visible damage?
options: It has gone out of fashion
It may have faded slightly in the sun over a summer
It may have reached the end of its service life
It has a scratch on the badge
questions.rationale: Follow manufacturer guidance.

questions.stem: What should you do if your gloves get soaked with chemicals?
options: Remove them safely and replace them
Keep wearing them until dry
Wipe them on your trousers
Wash them in the lineside drain and carry on
questions.rationale: Contaminated gloves can harm you.

questions.stem: Why should safety glasses fit properly?
options: Loose glasses look unprofessional
Tight glasses are more expensive
Fit does not matter
Gaps can let debris reach your eyes
questions.rationale: PPE must fit to protect.

questions.stem: What should you do if your safety glasses steam up and you cannot see?
options: Carry on working blind
Take them off near the line
Stop, clear them or use anti-fog glasses
Wipe them on your sleeve and carry on working
questions.rationale: You must be able to see trains and hazards.

questions.stem: What PPE helps protect against cuts when handling sharp materials?
options: Cut-resistant gloves
Woollen gloves
Latex gloves
No gloves
questions.rationale: Choose gloves for the hazard.

questions.stem: Why might you be asked to wear a lifejacket on some sites?
options: Because there is a risk of falling into water
Because it is cold
Because it is orange
Because it is required for all bridges
questions.rationale: Water hazards need suitable controls.

questions.stem: What is a harness used for in railway work?
options: Pulling trolleys along the rails
Fall protection when working at height
Carrying tools to site
Tying equipment to the fence
questions.rationale: Harnesses need correct use and anchor points.

questions.stem: Who should inspect fall-arrest equipment before use?
options: Nobody; it lasts for ever
The user, plus formal inspections as required
Only the manufacturer
Nobody, as harnesses last for the life of the user
questions.rationale: Check harnesses before each use.

questions.stem: Why should you not share ear plugs?
options: They are too expensive
They have names on them
For hygiene and fit reasons
They only work for one person
questions.rationale: Use your own hearing protection.

questions.stem: What should you do if your PPE is uncomfortable to the point you want to remove it?
options: Remove it while nobody is looking
Tell your supervisor so it can be changed
Wear it loosely
Cut parts off it so it is more comfortable
questions.rationale: Comfortable PPE is more likely to be worn.

questions.stem: What does 'PPE is the last resort' mean?
options: Other controls should be used first
PPE is the most important control
PPE is only used at the end of a shift
PPE is only for emergencies
questions.rationale: Remove or reduce hazards before relying on PPE.

questions.stem: Which of these is a better control than relying on hearing protection?
options: Wearing thicker ear defenders
Shouting louder
Using quieter equipment
Working faster
questions.rationale: Reduce noise at source where possible.

questions.stem: Why should hi-vis be stored properly when not in use?
options: To stop it being stolen
To keep it clean and in good condition
To keep it warm before putting it on
To stop it fading at night
questions.rationale: Look after PPE.

questions.stem: What should you do with PPE that is contaminated with oil?
options: Wear it anyway until the end of the week
Clean or replace it as instructed
Burn it on site
Throw it on the ballast
questions.rationale: Contaminated PPE may not protect you.

questions.stem: Why should you avoid wearing loose jewellery like chains on site?
options: It might be stolen
It reflects light into the eyes of approaching drivers
It can catch on equipment or moving parts
It is against fashion rules
questions.rationale: Entanglement can cause serious injury.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a face shield when grinding?
options: To keep your face warm during winter night shifts
To stop dust in the hair
To protect the face from sparks and fragments
To hide your identity
questions.rationale: Grinding throws hot particles.

questions.stem: Why is good fit important for safety boots?
options: Big boots are always safer
Poor fit causes trips and foot injuries
Tight boots are warmer
Fit does not matter as long as there is a toe cap
questions.rationale: Comfortable, well-fitting boots help you move safely.

questions.stem: What PPE might be needed when handling creosoted sleepers?
options: Only a hi-vis vest
Suitable gloves and protective clothing
Only sunglasses
Only a hi-vis vest and normal work gloves
questions.rationale: Creosote can irritate skin.

questions.stem: Why might sunscreen be part of personal equipment in summer?
options: To make hi-vis brighter
To protect against sunburn and skin damage
To make high-visibility clothing look brighter
To keep you warm
questions.rationale: Outdoor workers have high sun exposure.

questions.stem: What should you do if you lose your PPE during a shift?
options: Stop work on the line until it is replaced
Carry on without it
Borrow yellow hi-vis
Carry on without it until the end of the shift
questions.rationale: PPE must be worn as required.

questions.stem: Which of these PPE items protects against noise?
options: Safety boots
Hi-vis jacket
Ear defenders
Gloves
questions.rationale: Hearing protection reduces noise exposure.

questions.stem: What is the danger of wearing ear defenders all the time on site?
options: You may not hear warnings when you need to
They wear out quickly
They make you too warm
They wear out very quickly if worn all the time
questions.rationale: Use them when needed and plan warnings.

questions.stem: Why should hi-vis be worn even on closed lines inside a possession?
options: It is only a rule for open lines
Plant operators and drivers still need to see you
It is only a rule for open lines, not possessions
To show your employer
questions.rationale: Vehicles still move in possessions.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to carry a knife on site?
options: Open in your hand so it is ready to use
Tucked in your boot blade up
Loose in a tool bag
Closed or sheathed, in a pocket or holder
questions.rationale: Prevent cuts.

questions.stem: What should you do if a colleague's PPE looks faded and dirty?
options: Ignore it
Take a photo
Suggest they replace it
Report them for discipline
questions.rationale: Look out for each other.

questions.stem: What is Network Rail's alcohol limit for people working on its infrastructure?
options: 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
There is no limit if you feel fine
29 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood
questions.rationale: Network Rail's limit is much stricter than the drink-drive limit in England and Wales.

questions.stem: What is Network Rail's breath alcohol limit for its staff and contractors?
options: 35 micrograms per 100 ml of breath
13 micrograms per 100 ml of breath
22 micrograms per 100 ml of breath
50 micrograms per 100 ml of breath
questions.rationale: 13 µg/100 ml breath is equivalent to the 29 mg/100 ml blood limit.

questions.stem: How does Network Rail's alcohol limit compare with the drink-drive limit in England and Wales?
options: It is the same
It is much lower
It is higher
There is no railway limit
questions.rationale: The drink-drive limit is 80 mg per 100 ml of blood. The railway limit is 29 mg.

questions.stem: Roughly how much alcohol might take someone over Network Rail's limit?
options: About 6 units spread over the evening
Under about 1.5 units, depending on the person
Around 6 units spread over the evening, if you eat as well
Only spirits count towards the limit
questions.rationale: The limit is very low. The safest approach is not to drink before work.

questions.stem: Under which Act is it a criminal offence to be unfit through drink or drugs while doing safety-critical work on the railway?
options: The Road Traffic Act 1988
The Data Protection Act 2018
The Transport and Works Act 1992
The Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003, Part 4
questions.rationale: Being unfit through drink or drugs while doing safety-critical railway work is a criminal offence.

questions.stem: Which of these is a type of drugs and alcohol test used on Network Rail infrastructure?
options: Testing only if you volunteer
Testing once in your career
Random unannounced testing
Testing only of managers
questions.rationale: Testing includes pre-appointment, random, for-cause and post-incident testing.

questions.stem: When might 'for-cause' testing be carried out?
options: Every Monday morning before the first shift of the week starts
When a manager suspects someone may be impaired
Every Monday morning before work starts
Only after a worker returns from holiday
questions.rationale: For-cause testing is triggered by reasonable suspicion.

questions.stem: When might 'post-incident' testing be carried out?
options: Only after an accident in which someone was seriously hurt or killed
After an accident, near miss or unsafe act
Only after an accident where someone died
Only if the person involved asks for one
questions.rationale: People involved in incidents may be tested.

questions.stem: What is pre-appointment testing?
options: A test carried out at the end of a person's employment
A test carried out on passengers at stations
A test carried out on train drivers only
A test before someone starts a safety-critical role
questions.rationale: New and transferring staff are tested before starting safety-critical work.

questions.stem: How is refusing a drugs and alcohol test usually treated?
options: As a negative result
As if the test were positive
As a minor issue if the person gives a good reason
As an automatic pass
questions.rationale: Refusal has the same consequences as failing.

questions.stem: Under Network Rail's updated policy, how long may a PTS holder lose their PTS and Sentinel card after a positive test?
options: One week
Five years
Six months
It is never removed
questions.rationale: Network Rail's updated standard revokes PTS and cancels the Sentinel card for five years.

questions.stem: According to Network Rail, what minimum proportion of safety-critical and sponsored staff should be randomly tested each year?
options: At least 1% of staff in each calendar year
At least 5% of staff in each financial year
Every member of staff every single month
At least 20% on a rolling 12-month basis
questions.rationale: Random testing aims to cover at least 20% of these staff each year.

questions.stem: Which drugs were added to Network Rail's testing panel under its updated policy?
options: Paracetamol and ibuprofen
Caffeine and nicotine
Tramadol and ketamine
Antibiotics and vitamins
questions.rationale: The panel was extended, and the cocaine cut-off was lowered.

questions.stem: How long before attending an initial PTS course must a drugs and alcohol test have been carried out?
options: No more than 3 years before
Any time in the past
No more than 3 years before the course
No more than 3 months before
questions.rationale: Training providers check D&A and medical requirements on Sentinel.

questions.stem: Can you go to work the morning after a heavy night of drinking?
options: Yes, because a night's sleep removes the alcohol
Yes, as long as you drink strong coffee first
Yes, because a full night's sleep removes the alcohol from your body
Only if you are free of alcohol, which can take many hours
questions.rationale: Alcohol leaves the body slowly. Sleep, coffee and showers do not speed it up.

questions.stem: Which of these speeds up how fast your body removes alcohol?
options: Nothing; only time removes alcohol
Drinking strong coffee or energy drinks
Taking a cold shower
Eating a big breakfast
questions.rationale: The liver processes alcohol at a fairly fixed rate.

questions.stem: What should you do if you are prescribed medicine that may cause drowsiness?
options: Stop taking it without telling your doctor or anyone at work
Tell your sponsor or manager and get advice about safety-critical work
Stop taking it without telling your doctor, sponsor or anyone else at work
Double the dose so the course is finished more quickly
questions.rationale: Some medicines affect alertness. Declare them as your employer requires.

questions.stem: Can over-the-counter medicines affect your fitness for track work?
options: Yes, some can cause drowsiness or affect concentration
No, only prescription medicines can affect you
No, only medicines prescribed by a doctor can affect you
Only if you take them late in the evening
questions.rationale: Read the labels and ask a pharmacist.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a colleague may be impaired?
options: Arriving early and helping to unload the van
Asking several questions during the briefing
Slurred speech, poor coordination or smelling of alcohol
Arriving early and offering to help unload the van
questions.rationale: If you suspect impairment, tell the COSS or supervisor.

questions.stem: What should you do if you think a colleague is under the influence on site?
options: Ignore it unless they start making obvious mistakes
Cover for them
Let them work in the cess only
Tell the COSS or supervisor straight away
questions.rationale: An impaired person is a danger to everyone.

questions.stem: Why are drugs and alcohol especially dangerous for track workers?
options: They make orange PPE look less visible to drivers
They make orange PPE look less visible to drivers at night
They change the line speed set for the area
They slow reactions and impair judgement near trains
questions.rationale: Even small amounts can affect your ability to react.

questions.stem: Can cannabis affect you the day after use?
options: Yes, effects and test results can last for some time
No, the effects wear off within a few minutes
No, the effects wear off completely within a few minutes
Only if it was taken together with alcohol
questions.rationale: Drugs can stay in the body and affect you long after use.

questions.stem: Where are drugs and alcohol test results recorded for Sentinel card holders?
options: On social media
On the Sentinel database
On your car registration
Nowhere
questions.rationale: Records are stored securely on Sentinel.

questions.stem: What is the Drug and Alcohol Support Programme for?
options: To sell approved home testing kits to railway staff
To support people who voluntarily disclose a problem
To sell home testing kits to railway staff
To train lookouts to spot impaired colleagues
questions.rationale: Voluntary disclosure can lead to support and active monitoring.

questions.stem: What is 'active monitoring' in drugs and alcohol policy?
options: Watching CCTV of stations to spot impaired passengers
Monitoring train speeds to spot impaired drivers
Extra testing for people who disclosed misuse and got support
Watching CCTV of stations to spot passengers who appear to be impaired
questions.rationale: It supports people returning to work safely.

questions.stem: What does 'fit for duty' mean?
options: Having the right paperwork, whatever your health
Arriving on time at the start of each shift
Having the right paperwork in date, whatever your health on the day
Being physically and mentally able to work safely
questions.rationale: Fitness includes alertness, health and freedom from drugs and alcohol.

questions.stem: Which of these can make you unfit for duty?
options: Wearing clean, well-fitting high-visibility clothing
Having a full night's sleep before the shift
Drinking plenty of water during the shift
Fatigue, illness, drugs, alcohol or certain medicines
questions.rationale: Tell your supervisor if you are not fit.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a railway medical for track workers?
options: To check you are fit enough to take part in sports
To check you meet the health standard for safety-critical work
To check that you are fit enough to take part in sports at weekends
To test whether you need glasses for reading documents
questions.rationale: Medicals cover things like vision, hearing and general health.

questions.stem: Why are eyesight and hearing checked in railway medicals?
options: You must be able to see and hear trains and warnings
To decide which shift pattern suits you best
To decide which shift pattern and which role suits you best
To choose which colour of PPE you wear
questions.rationale: Detecting trains and warnings depends on these senses.

questions.stem: What should you do if your health changes in a way that could affect your safety?
options: Keep it to yourself until your next medical
Tell your sponsor or manager
Only tell your friends
Wait for your next medical
questions.rationale: Health changes can affect your fitness for track work.

questions.stem: What does 'fatigue' mean in a work context?
options: Being bored with repetitive tasks at work
Being hungry because you missed a meal
Tiredness that reduces your alertness and performance
Being bored with repetitive tasks during long shifts
questions.rationale: Fatigue is a major safety risk on the railway.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign of fatigue?
options: Feeling alert and focused on the task
Yawning, slow reactions and poor concentration
Feeling alert and focused on the task in hand
Speaking clearly in the briefing
questions.rationale: Recognise the signs in yourself and others.

questions.stem: Under Sentinel Scheme Rules, when should you not report for duty on the managed infrastructure?
options: Within 12 hours of a previous shift on it, unless assessed and controlled
On any weekend, unless your sponsor has given written permission
On any weekend, unless your sponsor has given you written permission to work
If you have slept for more than eight hours since your last shift
questions.rationale: This rule aims to prevent 'double-shifting'.

questions.stem: What is 'double-shifting'?
options: Working under two COSSs at the same time on one site
Going straight from one shift into another without enough rest
Working under two different COSSs at the same time on one site
Working with two lookouts protecting the same group
questions.rationale: Double-shifting causes dangerous fatigue.

questions.stem: Under Sentinel rules, which working hours limits apply?
options: The shortest of the legal, infrastructure or sponsor limits
The longest of the legal, infrastructure or sponsor limits
Only the limits set by your Primary Sponsor
No limits apply to contract workers
questions.rationale: You must not exceed the strictest applicable limit.

questions.stem: Under Network Rail's fatigue standard, what happens when someone works more than 60 hours in 7 rolling days?
options: A fatigue assessment and management plan with controls is needed
Nothing, as long as the person says they feel fine
They receive a bonus payment for the extra hours
Nothing at all, as long as the person says that they feel absolutely fine
questions.rationale: This is a trigger condition. Controls include no lookout duties and no working alone.

questions.stem: When did Network Rail's newer fatigue standard come fully into force?
options: January 2000
October 2022
March 2010
It has not been introduced
questions.rationale: It came into full force on 29 October 2022 and applies to everyone working on Network Rail infrastructure.

questions.stem: How does Network Rail's newer fatigue standard manage working hours?
options: It bans all overtime for everyone working on the railway
It sets no rules and leaves hours to each employer
It only covers train drivers and signallers
It uses trigger conditions that require assessment and controls
questions.rationale: Instead of fixed limits only, triggers require mitigating actions.

questions.stem: Why does travel time matter when thinking about fatigue?
options: It does not matter, as travel is not work
It only matters for professional drivers
It does not matter, as travel time is not counted as work
Long journeys add to tiredness before and after a shift
questions.rationale: Sentinel rules say you must not be fatigued by excessive travel or work.

questions.stem: What should you do if you feel too tired to work safely?
options: Take a quick nap in the cess between trains and carry on
Take a quick nap in the cess between trains
Tell your supervisor or COSS and stay off the line
Hide it so that you do not lose the shift
questions.rationale: Fatigue reduces your ability to react to trains.

questions.stem: Why are night shifts linked to higher fatigue risk?
options: Trains are much louder at night and keep people awake
Trains are much louder at night and the noise keeps people awake on site
The body clock makes people sleepy at night, especially early morning
Lookouts are allowed to sleep between trains at night
questions.rationale: Plan rest and watch for fatigue on nights.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for being fit for work?
options: Only the sponsor who employs them
Every individual, supported by their sponsor
Only the COSS in charge of the group on site
Only the COSS in charge on site
questions.rationale: Sentinel rules make each person responsible for being fit for work.

questions.stem: Which of these personal circumstances should you report if it affects your ability to work safely?
options: Buying a new car for travelling to sites
Changing your mobile phone number
Buying a new car for travelling to and from sites
A serious lack of sleep due to a family emergency
questions.rationale: Report anything that may affect your ability to work safely.

questions.stem: Is it acceptable to drink alcohol during a meal break on a shift?
options: Yes, one small drink with food is fine
Yes, if the break is longer than an hour
No, you must not drink alcohol while on duty
Yes, one small drink with food is acceptable
questions.rationale: Alcohol is not allowed at work.

questions.stem: Why might energy drinks not be a safe fix for fatigue?
options: They are too sweet to drink during a shift
They contain alcohol, which is not allowed at work
They contain alcohol, which is not allowed
They may mask tiredness without restoring alertness
questions.rationale: Only proper rest fixes fatigue.

questions.stem: What is a lifesaving rule about drugs and alcohol when driving for work?
options: Drive slowly if you have had a drink
Drive only on quiet roads after drinking
Drive slowly and use quiet roads if you have had a drink
Never drive under the influence of drink or drugs
questions.rationale: Network Rail's driving lifesaving rules include never driving under the influence.

questions.stem: Why are driving rules part of track safety?
options: Anyone who drives to site must also hold PTS
Some road vehicles on site run on the rails
Anyone who drives to site must also hold a PTS certificate
Road journeys to and from site are a major risk to workers
questions.rationale: Fatigue after shifts makes driving home dangerous.

questions.stem: What should you do if a colleague who seems tired plans to drive home after a long night shift?
options: Let them go, as driving home is their own business
Let them go, as driving home is their own business once the shift is over
Suggest they drive fast so they get home sooner
Urge them to rest or use other transport, and tell a supervisor
questions.rationale: Fatigued driving can kill.

questions.stem: Which of these increases the effects of alcohol?
options: Combining it with some medicines or drugs
Drinking water after the alcohol
Eating a meal at the same time
Drinking a pint of water after the alcohol
questions.rationale: Mixing substances can be very dangerous.

questions.stem: What is the safest approach to alcohol before a shift?
options: Drink only beer, as it is weaker than wine or spirits
Drink only beer, as it is weaker than wine or spirits and wears off faster
Drink only the night before, as sleep clears it
Do not drink in the hours before work, so you are alcohol-free
questions.rationale: Plan your drinking around your shifts.

questions.stem: You were out at a party until 2 am and start a shift at 7 am. What is the safest action?
options: Drink strong coffee on the way in and start work as normal at seven o'clock
Drink strong coffee on the way in and start as normal
Assume alcohol may still be in your system and tell your supervisor
Take a cold shower, then go in and start as normal
questions.rationale: Alcohol takes many hours to leave the body.

questions.stem: Your doctor prescribes strong painkillers that may cause drowsiness. You have a shift tomorrow. What should you do?
options: Tell your sponsor or manager first and follow their medication process
Take them as prescribed and work as normal without telling anyone
Do not take them and work in pain so you stay fully alert
Take half the dose and hope it does not make you drowsy
questions.rationale: Declare medication that could affect your work.

questions.stem: A colleague tells you they smoked cannabis last night but feel fine. What should you do?
options: Keep their secret, as they say they feel completely fine
Let them work in the cess where it is a bit safer
Keep their secret, as they say they feel fine and it was the night before
Urge them to tell the supervisor, and raise it yourself if they will not
questions.rationale: Drugs can affect performance and safety without people realising.

questions.stem: You are selected for a random test at the start of a shift. What should you do?
options: Refuse and leave
Ask to do it next week
Co-operate with the test
Drink lots of water first
questions.rationale: Refusal is treated as a positive result.

questions.stem: After a near miss with a train, the COSS says you will be tested. Why?
options: Post-incident testing is part of the drugs and alcohol policy
Because you are being blamed for the near miss
Because you happened to be picked at random that day
Because you are being blamed for the near miss and must prove your innocence
questions.rationale: Post-incident tests help rule out impairment as a cause.

questions.stem: Which of these is the best way to manage fatigue before a night shift?
options: Plan sleep beforehand, for example a nap in the afternoon
Stay awake all day so you are tired enough to sleep later
Drink alcohol in the morning to help you get to sleep
Work another job during the day to use the time
questions.rationale: Good sleep planning reduces fatigue.

questions.stem: Which of these can affect your fitness for duty as much as alcohol?
options: Clean PPE
A good breakfast
Severe fatigue
A short walk
questions.rationale: Being awake for very long periods impairs performance like alcohol.

questions.stem: Why should you tell your manager about a long commute before an early shift?
options: It affects how rested you are and the fatigue risk
So you can claim mileage for the journey
So that you can claim mileage for the journey
It does not matter, as long as you arrive
questions.rationale: Fatigue risk includes travel time.

questions.stem: Which statement about mental health and railway safety is correct?
options: Stress and poor mental health can affect concentration and should be raised
Mental health never affects safety as long as you are physically fit
You should hide any stress at work so you are not removed from duty
Only physical health matters for safety-critical work on track
questions.rationale: Seek support and tell your manager if it affects your work.

questions.stem: Why should you eat properly before a long shift?
options: Low energy and hunger reduce concentration
It makes you heavier and more stable
Eating a large meal makes you more alert for hours
It speeds up alcohol removal
questions.rationale: Look after yourself to stay alert.

questions.stem: How can very hot weather affect your fitness for track work?
options: Heat stress can cause tiredness, confusion and fainting
Heat has no effect as long as you wear light clothing
Heat has no effect if you wear light clothing
Heat improves your hearing in the open air
questions.rationale: Drink water, take breaks and watch for heat illness.

questions.stem: How can very cold weather affect your fitness for track work?
options: Cold makes you move faster and react sooner
Cold makes you move faster and react more quickly
Cold improves your eyesight in winter
Cold can slow your reactions and make you clumsy
questions.rationale: Wear suitable layers and take warm breaks.

questions.stem: What should you do if you start to feel faint while on the lineside?
options: Stop, move to a safe place away from the line and tell someone
Lie down in the cess until the feeling passes
Keep working and drink some water when you can
Keep working and drink some water when you get the chance later on
questions.rationale: Fainting near the line could be fatal.

questions.stem: Which of these would most likely make you unfit to act as a lookout?
options: Wearing glasses that correct short-sightedness
Having had very little sleep in the last 24 hours
Wearing glasses that correct your vision
Having a cold drink just before starting
questions.rationale: Lookouts need full concentration.

questions.stem: Why should you not drive straight home after a long night shift if you are very tired?
options: Fatigue greatly increases the risk of crashing
Traffic is heavier in the early morning
Traffic is much heavier in the early morning rush
It is illegal to drive at dawn after work
questions.rationale: Rest first or use other transport.

questions.stem: Which statement about alcohol and the next day is correct?
options: Alcohol is always gone after sleep
Alcohol is always gone after a full night's sleep
Food removes alcohol overnight
You can still be over the limit the next morning
questions.rationale: Allow plenty of time.

questions.stem: Who carries out drugs and alcohol testing for railway workers?
options: The driver of any train that passes the work site
The lookout, as part of their duties on site
Approved testing providers acting for employers and Network Rail
The driver of any train that passes the work site during the shift
questions.rationale: Testing follows strict procedures.

questions.stem: What should you do if you accidentally took a medicine that makes you drowsy before a shift?
options: Tell your supervisor and do not go on or near the line
Go to work and say nothing unless you feel ill
Ask to work as a lookout instead, as it is less physical
Ask to work as a lookout, as it is less physical
questions.rationale: Being honest keeps everyone safe.

questions.stem: Why do safety-critical workers have stricter alcohol rules than drivers on public roads?
options: Railway workers are known to drink more than others
Trains are slower than cars, so reactions matter more
It is just a tradition with no real safety reason
Mistakes near trains can be instantly fatal for many people
questions.rationale: The consequences of impairment on the railway are severe.

questions.stem: Which of these actions is most likely to reduce fatigue risk across a team?
options: Scheduling double shifts to finish work sooner
Planning shifts with enough rest between them
Allowing unlimited overtime for volunteers
Removing breaks to shorten the shift
questions.rationale: Good rostering is a key fatigue control.

questions.stem: Which statement about 'microsleeps' is correct?
options: They only ever happen when you are lying down in bed
They only ever happen when you are lying down in bed at home at night
Very tired people can fall asleep for seconds without knowing
They only affect people who drive road vehicles
questions.rationale: A few seconds without attention can be fatal near trains.

questions.stem: If you feel your eyes closing while on site, what should you do?
options: Splash cold water on your face and carry on
Stop work, get to a safe place and tell the COSS
Ignore it, as it will pass in a few minutes
Take a short nap in the four-foot
questions.rationale: These are serious fatigue warning signs.

questions.stem: How can poor fitness for duty affect the whole group?
options: It only affects how much the group is paid for the shift
One person's mistake can put everyone in danger
It only affects how much the group is paid
It has no effect if the others are alert
questions.rationale: Track safety relies on everyone being alert.

questions.stem: Which of these is the best reason for honest disclosure of a drug or alcohol problem?
options: Support may be available and it keeps everyone safe
It guarantees you a promotion once you have recovered
It guarantees you a promotion afterwards
It removes the need for future medicals
questions.rationale: Voluntary disclosure can lead to help.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to handle a celebration on the evening before an early shift?
options: Drink, but switch to water after midnight
Avoid drinking so you are fully fit for work
Drink only soft drinks with spirits
Drink lots of water with alcohol
questions.rationale: Plan ahead to stay within the rules.

questions.stem: What might happen if you test positive at work?
options: Nothing happens as long as you apologise to the COSS straight away
You are given a verbal warning and can carry on with the shift
You are moved to lookout duty for the rest of the shift
You are removed from safety work, and PTS and Sentinel can be withdrawn
questions.rationale: Consequences are serious and can include long bans.

questions.stem: What is the most important reason for random testing?
options: To catch people out for the managers' benefit
To deter misuse and help keep the railway safe
To collect data that can be used for marketing
To check what people have eaten that day
questions.rationale: Random testing is a deterrent.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a reason you could be unfit for duty?
options: Taking a sedating medicine
Being hungover
Being extremely tired
Wearing the correct PPE
questions.rationale: PPE does not affect fitness for duty.

questions.stem: What does 'safety-critical work' mean?
options: Work that is done in an office away from the line
Work where mistakes could cause serious harm to people
Work that is paid at a higher rate than others
Work that is only done by managers and supervisors
questions.rationale: Track work is safety-critical.

questions.stem: What should you do if you are recovering from an illness and still feel weak?
options: Work alone so that you do not slow the others down
Tell your manager before returning to track work
Work alone so you do not slow others down
Take extra painkillers to get through it
questions.rationale: Only return when fit.

questions.stem: How can poor sleep at home over several days affect your work?
options: It improves concentration on the next shift
It has no effect as long as you feel fine
It only affects people who drive for work
It builds up a 'sleep debt' that reduces alertness
questions.rationale: Sleep debt is a fatigue risk.

questions.stem: Who should you speak to if you are worried about a colleague's drinking?
options: Nobody, as it is their private business
Social media, so others can help them
Your supervisor or a confidential support service
Nobody, as their drinking is their own private business
questions.rationale: Raising concerns can save lives.

questions.stem: Why should you avoid taking someone else's prescription medicine?
options: It is cheaper to buy the same medicine for yourself
Other people's medicine is often past its use-by date
It may affect you unexpectedly and breach the drugs policy
It might be a different colour or shape from your own
questions.rationale: Only take medicine prescribed for you.

questions.stem: What does it mean to be 'under the influence' at work?
options: Being strongly influenced by your manager's opinions about how to work
Having alcohol or drugs in your system that affect or could affect your work
Being on a long shift that has gone past its planned finishing time
Wearing a headset that plays music while you are working
questions.rationale: The railway has strict limits.

questions.stem: Which statement about fatigue and lookout duties is correct?
options: Fatigue is not important for lookouts
People who are fatigued must not act as lookouts
Lookouts can work longer hours
Lookout duties are fine for tired people as they are not physical
questions.rationale: Fatigue controls specifically restrict lookout duties.

questions.stem: Which of these factors can increase fatigue?
options: Regular breaks taken throughout the shift
Regular breaks taken throughout every part of the shift
Long shifts, night work, long travel and poor sleep
Short shifts with plenty of rest days
questions.rationale: Fatigue builds from many factors together.

questions.stem: Why should you not work alone if fatigue trigger conditions are met?
options: Nobody is there to notice if your alertness drops
It is cheaper for the sponsor to have people work in pairs
It is cheaper to have people work in pairs
It is a union rule for all fatigued workers
questions.rationale: Controls for fatigue include no working alone.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a fatigue risk assessment?
options: To decide which rate of pay applies to night work
To pick who will lead the next shift
To choose PPE for the coming season
To identify fatigue risks and set controls
questions.rationale: Assessments help manage working patterns safely.

questions.stem: A colleague arrives on site smelling strongly of alcohol. The COSS has not noticed. What should you do?
options: Stay quiet
Lend them mints
Tell the COSS straight away
Ask them to stay at the back
questions.rationale: Impaired people must not work on the railway.

questions.stem: What is the drink-drive blood alcohol limit in England and Wales?
options: 29 mg per 100 ml of blood, the same as the railway limit
50 mg per 100 ml of blood, the same as in Scotland
80 mg per 100 ml of blood
There is no fixed limit for drivers in England and Wales
questions.rationale: Network Rail's 29 mg limit is far lower than the 80 mg drink-drive limit.

questions.stem: Which is stricter: Network Rail's alcohol limit or the England and Wales drink-drive limit?
options: The drink-drive limit, which is lower than any work rule
They are exactly the same, set by the same law
Network Rail's limit
Neither, because there are no limits for track workers
questions.rationale: 29 mg/100 ml compared with 80 mg/100 ml.

questions.stem: What is 'impairment'?
options: A reduced ability to work safely
A legal term for being over the drink-drive limit only
A type of medical certificate for railway workers
A short break taken during a long shift
questions.rationale: Drugs, alcohol, medicines, fatigue and illness can all impair you.

questions.stem: Which of these can impair you without alcohol or drugs?
options: Wearing new safety boots
Severe tiredness
Drinking plenty of water
Taking a short rest break
questions.rationale: Fatigue impairs judgement and reactions.

questions.stem: A colleague says they 'only had two pints at lunch'. They are about to go on the line. What should you do?
options: Let them work, as two pints is under the drink-drive limit
Suggest they drink coffee before going on the line
Tell the COSS straight away
Ask them to work in the cess rather than the four-foot
questions.rationale: Alcohol at work breaks the rules and two pints may exceed 29 mg.

questions.stem: Why is 'morning-after' drinking risk so common?
options: Alcohol becomes stronger overnight in the body
People underestimate how long alcohol stays in the body
Breath tests are more sensitive in the morning
Alcohol becomes stronger overnight while you are asleep in bed
questions.rationale: Alcohol leaves the body slowly, roughly one unit per hour for many people.

questions.stem: Roughly how fast does the body remove alcohol for many people?
options: About five units per hour
About one unit per hour
All of it within one hour of sleep
About one unit per day
questions.rationale: It varies by person, so the safest choice is not to drink before shifts.

questions.stem: Which medicines should you be most cautious about before track work?
options: Vitamins and mineral supplements
Plasters and antiseptic cream
Throat sweets
Ones labelled 'may cause drowsiness'
questions.rationale: Check labels and ask a pharmacist.

questions.stem: Who can advise whether a medicine is safe for safety-critical work?
options: A colleague who has taken the same medicine before
The internet forum for track workers
A doctor or pharmacist, with your employer's process
The driver of the next train
questions.rationale: Get proper advice and declare as required.

questions.stem: What does a 'for-cause' test protect against?
options: Someone claiming too much overtime
Someone working while possibly impaired
Someone losing their Sentinel card
Someone parking in the wrong place
questions.rationale: It is triggered by reasonable suspicion.

questions.stem: Which statement about prescribed medication and drug tests is correct?
options: Declare it, as it may show up in a test
Prescribed medication never shows up in tests
You must stop taking it before every shift
You only need to declare it if you feel unwell
questions.rationale: Declaring medication helps interpret results and protects you.

questions.stem: What is 'presenteeism' in safety terms?
options: Arriving early before every shift
Being present at every briefing
Coming to work when unfit to work safely
Staying late to help the group
questions.rationale: Working while unwell or impaired puts everyone at risk.

questions.stem: What should you do if you have not slept because of a newborn baby at home?
options: Come in and say nothing so you do not lose pay
Tell your supervisor before working
Drink energy drinks and act as lookout
Work a double shift to make up time later
questions.rationale: Lack of sleep affects safety. Report it.

questions.stem: Which of these is a fatigue control a manager might use?
options: Longer shifts with fewer breaks
More night shifts in a row
Working alone for longer
Rest breaks and no lookout duties
questions.rationale: Controls aim to reduce the risk from tiredness.

questions.stem: Why is the body clock important for night workers?
options: Alertness is naturally lowest in the early hours
It makes people more alert at 3 am
It only affects people over 50 who work at night
It resets after one night shift
questions.rationale: Plan extra care for the early morning low point.

questions.stem: What is the safest way to change from day to night shifts?
options: Stay awake for 24 hours first
Drink alcohol to help sleep
Plan rest and sleep to adjust
Do both shifts on the same day
questions.rationale: Good planning reduces fatigue.

questions.stem: Why might a long hot shift increase the risk of a mistake?
options: Heat and dehydration reduce concentration
Heat makes trains go faster on hot rails
Hot weather speeds up reactions
PPE works better when it is hot
questions.rationale: Drink water and take breaks in the shade.

questions.stem: What should you do if you notice a colleague sweating heavily and confused on a hot day?
options: Tell them to carry on and drink later
Get them to a cool safe place and get help
Give them an energy drink and leave them
Ask them to act as lookout instead
questions.rationale: These may be signs of heat illness.

questions.stem: Why are railway medicals repeated at intervals?
options: Health can change over time
To raise money for training providers
To check you still remember the rules
To renew your Sentinel photograph
questions.rationale: Fitness must be maintained.

questions.stem: What is colour vision important for on the railway?
options: Choosing the right PPE size
Reading the timetable on station screens
Matching tools to their cases
Recognising signals and coloured warnings
questions.rationale: Some roles need specific colour vision standards.

questions.stem: Why is good hearing important for track workers?
options: To hear music during breaks
To hear trains, horns and warnings
To hear the signaller's phone ringing
To hear wildlife near the track
questions.rationale: Hearing is checked in medicals.

questions.stem: What should you do if your hearing gets worse between medicals?
options: Tell your manager or sponsor
Wait until your next medical
Ask the lookout to shout
Wear ear defenders to hide it
questions.rationale: Changes in fitness must be reported.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign someone may be under the influence of drugs?
options: Asking for a copy of the briefing
Wearing their hi-vis fully fastened
Unusual behaviour, dilated pupils or poor coordination
Asking for a printed copy of the briefing to keep
questions.rationale: Report concerns; do not try to diagnose.

questions.stem: Should you confront a colleague you think is impaired?
options: Yes, and test them yourself with a breathalyser
Yes, and send them home without telling anyone
No; report it to the COSS or supervisor
Yes, and take their Sentinel card away
questions.rationale: Let the proper process deal with it.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the drugs and alcohol policy?
options: Catching people to discipline them
Keeping everyone safe
Reducing the cost of training
Making sure people arrive on time
questions.rationale: It protects workers, passengers and the public.

questions.stem: What is the safest response to being offered alcohol at a site celebration?
options: Accept one small drink only
Refuse while you are on duty
Accept if the COSS also drinks
Accept if your shift ends soon
questions.rationale: No alcohol at work.

questions.stem: What is a 'safety-critical' worker's legal duty about alcohol and drugs?
options: To report other workers' drinking only
To be tested once in their career
Not to be unfit through them while working
To drink only after 6 pm
questions.rationale: It is a criminal offence to be unfit through drink or drugs in safety-critical work.

questions.stem: Which of these could affect your balance near the line?
options: A new haircut
An inner ear infection
A clean hi-vis jacket
A full water bottle
questions.rationale: Report health issues that could affect safety.

questions.stem: What should a diabetic worker do to stay fit for duty?
options: Skip meals during the shift so they stay alert
Avoid telling their sponsor
Follow medical advice and keep supplies with them
Rely on colleagues to notice
questions.rationale: Manage conditions and declare them as required.

questions.stem: Why might you be asked about medical conditions in a railway medical?
options: To decide your pay rate and shift pattern
To choose your shift pattern
To share with the train company
Some conditions can affect safety on the line
questions.rationale: Medical information is used to assess fitness.

questions.stem: If you feel dizzy while walking in the cess, what should you do?
options: Lean on the conductor rail
Stop, move away from the line and tell someone
Keep walking slowly
Lean on the conductor rail until the feeling passes
questions.rationale: Get to safety and get help.

questions.stem: What is the danger of mixing alcohol with sleeping tablets?
options: They cancel each other out
The effects can combine and last longer
Alcohol stops tablets working
There is no effect if you sleep afterwards
questions.rationale: Mixing can be dangerous.

questions.stem: What does 'zero tolerance' to drugs at work mean on the railway?
options: Any illegal drug use is not accepted
Small amounts are fine at weekends
Only drugs taken at work count
Only managers are tested
questions.rationale: Illegal drugs are not tolerated in safety-critical work.

questions.stem: Who might carry out a random drugs and alcohol test on site?
options: Any member of the public
The lookout
An approved collection officer
The driver of a passing train
questions.rationale: Tests follow strict procedures.

questions.stem: What should you do if you feel stressed and it is affecting your concentration?
options: Talk to your manager or a support service
Work longer hours so you have less time to think
Work longer to forget it
Drink to relax before work
questions.rationale: Support is available.

questions.stem: Why is caffeine not a cure for fatigue?
options: It is banned on the railway
It only masks tiredness for a while
It makes you sleep instantly
It contains alcohol
questions.rationale: Only sleep fixes fatigue.

questions.stem: What is the best way to prepare for an early start?
options: Stay up late and nap in the van
Drink energy drinks all night
Get to bed early enough for a full sleep
Skip sleep and start early to get it over with
questions.rationale: Plan sleep around shifts.

questions.stem: Why should you tell your sponsor about a second job?
options: So they can take a share of the pay
So they can check your references
It is not needed
So total hours and rest can be managed
questions.rationale: Hours across jobs affect fatigue.

questions.stem: What is 'sleep inertia'?
options: Falling asleep at work
A type of sleeping tablet
Grogginess just after waking
A long sleep after nights
questions.rationale: Allow time to become alert after naps.

questions.stem: Why should you not start safety-critical work immediately after a nap?
options: You will be too energetic
Naps are not allowed
You will forget the briefing
You may be groggy for a short time
questions.rationale: Give yourself time to wake properly.

questions.stem: Which of these increases fatigue risk the most?
options: Several night shifts in a row with little sleep
A single day shift after a good sleep
A short walk before work
A balanced breakfast before the first shift
questions.rationale: Fatigue builds up over consecutive nights.

questions.stem: What should you do if a colleague keeps nodding off in the van before work?
options: Let them rest and wake them at the site
Give them a strong coffee
Raise it with the COSS
Ask them to be lookout
questions.rationale: They may be unfit for duty.

questions.stem: What does fitness for duty include besides drugs and alcohol?
options: Having a car
Owning the latest phone
Living near the site
Health, fatigue and wellbeing
questions.rationale: Fitness covers many factors.

questions.stem: Is a valid medical certificate enough to show you are fit on a particular day?
options: Yes, it covers every day until it expires
No; you must also be fit on the day
Yes, if it was issued this year
Yes, if your sponsor agrees
questions.rationale: Your condition on the day matters.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of 'post-incident' testing for the people involved?
options: To decide who pays for damage
To find out who was in charge
To check their competences are still valid
To check whether impairment played a part
questions.rationale: It supports a full investigation.

questions.stem: What is the Sentinel scheme?
options: The system recording the identity and competences of NR infrastructure workers
An app that shows the live train timetable to track workers on site
An automatic warning system that alerts groups to approaching trains
An automatic warning system that alerts groups of track workers to approaching trains
questions.rationale: Sentinel helps make sure only competent, fit people work on the railway.

questions.stem: What is a Sentinel card?
options: A photo card linked to your record of competences
A bank card issued to all railway staff for pay
A free travel pass for use on passenger trains
A free travel pass for staff to use on passenger trains
questions.rationale: Your Sentinel card is often called your passport to work on the railway.

questions.stem: When must you carry your Sentinel card?
options: Only on your first day with a new sponsor or site
Only on your first day with a new sponsor or at a new site
Whenever you are on Network Rail managed infrastructure
Only on night shifts when there are more checks
questions.rationale: You must carry it and present it when asked.

questions.stem: What must you do if someone with authority asks to see your Sentinel card?
options: Refuse, it is private
Show it for checking
Show a photo of it
Show your driving licence instead
questions.rationale: Card checks confirm identity and competence.

questions.stem: Who is your 'Primary Sponsor' under Sentinel?
options: The organisation responsible for you and your Sentinel record
The train operating company that runs the most trains on the line
The landlord of the property where you live
The train operating company that runs the line
questions.rationale: The Primary Sponsor manages your competence, medical, D&A and safety.

questions.stem: Who pays for Sentinel cards under the scheme?
options: The sponsor
The individual worker
The government
The train company
questions.rationale: Issuing and paying for Sentinel cards is the sponsor's responsibility.

questions.stem: Can you lend your Sentinel card to a colleague?
options: No, it is for your use only
Yes, if they hold the same competences as you do
Yes, if they have PTS too
Yes, if they are a visitor
questions.rationale: Lending your card is a serious breach and could put lives at risk.

questions.stem: What should you do if you lose your Sentinel card?
